verses.text: Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
We always thank God for all of you and mention you in our prayers.
We remember your work produced by faith, your labor motivated by love, and your endurance grounded in hope in our Lord Jesus Christ before our God and Father.
Brothers and sisters loved by God, we know that he has chosen you.
Our Good News came to you not just in words but with power, with the Holy Spirit, and with deep conviction. You know how we lived among you for your sake.
You became imitators of us and of the Lord. Though you suffered greatly, you welcomed the message with the joy the Holy Spirit gives.
So you became an example to all the believers in Macedonia and Achaia.
The Lord's message rang out from you—not only through Macedonia and Achaia, but everywhere people have heard about your faith in God. We don't need to say anything more.
People everywhere tell how you welcomed us and how you turned from idols to serve the living and true God
and to wait for his Son to come from heaven. God raised Jesus from the dead, and he rescues us from the coming judgment.
Brothers and sisters, you know our visit to you wasn't wasted.
Even after we had suffered and been mistreated in Philippi, as you know, we found courage in God to share his Good News with you despite strong opposition.
Our appeal didn't come from error, impure motives, or trickery.
Instead, God approved us and entrusted us with the Good News. So we speak to please God, who examines our hearts, not to please people.
As you know, we never used flattery or put on a show to cover greed. God is our witness.
We weren't looking for praise from people—not from you or anyone else—even though as Christ's apostles we could have made demands.
Instead, we were gentle among you, like a nursing mother tenderly caring for her own children.
We cared for you so deeply that we were glad to share with you not only God's Good News but our own lives too. You had become dear to us.
Brothers and sisters, you remember our hard work. We worked night and day so we wouldn't burden anyone while we shared God's Good News with you.
You and God are witnesses of how holy, just, and blameless we were toward you who believe.
You know how we encouraged, comforted, and urged each one of you, like a father with his children,
to live in a way worthy of God, who calls you into his own Kingdom and glory.
We also thank God constantly because when you received God's message from us, you welcomed it for what it truly is—not a human message but God's word, which is at work in you who believe.
Brothers and sisters, you became imitators of God's churches in Judea in Christ Jesus. You suffered the same things from your own people as they did from the Judeans,
who killed the Lord Jesus and the prophets, drove us out, and displease God by opposing everyone.
They try to stop us from speaking to the Gentiles so they might be saved. In this way they keep piling up their sins. But God's anger has finally come upon them.
Brothers and sisters, when we were separated from you for a short time in person—but never in heart—we tried all the harder, with great longing, to see you face to face.
We wanted to come to you. I, Paul, tried again and again, but Satan blocked our way.
After all, what is our hope, joy, or crown to celebrate? Isn't it you, standing before our Lord Jesus when he comes?
You are our glory and joy.
When we couldn't stand being apart from you any longer, we decided to stay behind alone in Athens
and send Timothy, our brother and God's co-worker in sharing the Good News about Christ, to strengthen and encourage you in your faith,
so no one would be shaken by these troubles. You know we're destined to face them.
Even when we were with you, we kept telling you that we would suffer. And, as you know, that's what happened.
That's why, when I couldn't stand it any longer, I sent Timothy to find out about your faith. I was afraid the tempter might have tempted you and made our work useless.
But Timothy has just returned from you with good news about your faith and love. He says you always remember us warmly and long to see us, just as we long to see you.
Brothers and sisters, because of your faith, we were encouraged about you in all our distress and trouble.
Now we can truly live, since you are standing firm in the Lord.
How can we thank God enough for you, for all the joy we feel because of you before our God?
Night and day we pray earnestly to see you again and to supply whatever is lacking in your faith.
May God our Father himself and our Lord Jesus clear the way for us to come to you.
May the Lord make your love grow and overflow for one another and for everyone, just as our love overflows for you.
May he strengthen your hearts so they are blameless and holy before our God and Father when our Lord Jesus comes with all his holy ones.
Finally, brothers and sisters, we ask and urge you in the Lord Jesus: keep living in a way that pleases God, just as we taught you. You're already doing this—keep growing in it.
You know the instructions we gave you through the Lord Jesus.
God wants you to be made holy: stay away from sexual immorality.
Each of you should learn to control your own body in holiness and honor,
not giving in to passionate desires like the Gentiles who don't know God.
In this matter, don't take advantage of or wrong a fellow believer. The Lord will punish such behavior, as we already warned and testified to you.
God didn't call us to impurity but to holiness.
Whoever rejects this instruction isn't rejecting a human being but God, who gives you his Holy Spirit.
About love for fellow believers, you don't need us to write you. God himself has taught you to love one another.
And you do love all the believers throughout Macedonia. Still, brothers and sisters, we urge you to keep growing in this love.
Make it your goal to live quietly, mind your own business, and work with your hands, just as we instructed you.
Then people outside the church will respect the way you live, and you won't have to depend on anyone.
Brothers and sisters, we don't want you to be uninformed about those who have died, so you won't grieve like people who have no hope.
We believe Jesus died and rose again. In the same way, God will bring with Jesus those who have died trusting him.
Here's what we tell you by the Lord's word: we who are alive and remain until the Lord comes will certainly not go ahead of those who have died.
The Lord himself will come down from heaven with a loud command, with the archangel's voice and God's trumpet. Those who died in Christ will rise first.
Then we who are still alive will be caught up with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air. And so we will be with the Lord forever.
So encourage one another with these words.
About the times and seasons, brothers and sisters, you don't need us to write to you.
You know very well that the day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night.
While people are saying, ‘Peace and safety,’ sudden destruction will come on them, like labor pains on a pregnant woman, and they won't escape.
But you, brothers and sisters, aren't in the dark, so that this day could catch you like a thief.
You are all children of light and children of the day. We don't belong to the night or the darkness.
So let's not sleep like everyone else. Let's stay alert and clear-minded.
Those who sleep, sleep at night, and those who get drunk, get drunk at night.
But since we belong to the day, let's be clear-minded, putting on faith and love as a breastplate and the hope of salvation as a helmet.
God didn't choose us for judgment but to receive salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ.
He died for us so that, whether we're awake or asleep, we may live together with him.
So encourage one another and build each other up, just as you're already doing.
Brothers and sisters, respect those who work among you, lead you in the Lord, and correct you.
Hold them in high regard and love because of their work. Live at peace with one another.
We urge you, brothers and sisters: warn those who are idle, encourage the discouraged, help the weak, and be patient with everyone.
Make sure no one pays back evil for evil. Always pursue what is good for one another and for everyone.
Always be joyful.
Never stop praying.
Give thanks in every situation, because this is God's will for you in Christ Jesus.
Don't put out the Spirit's fire.
Don't treat prophecies with contempt.
Test everything. Hold on to what is good.
Stay away from every kind of evil.
May the God of peace himself make you completely holy. May your whole spirit, soul, and body be kept blameless when our Lord Jesus Christ comes.
The one who calls you is faithful, and he will do it.
Brothers and sisters, pray for us.
Greet all the believers with a holy kiss.
I charge you before the Lord to have this letter read to all the brothers and sisters.
May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.
